senses.gloss: (cmp. בקע) to split; to burst; to break forth, escape.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 32">Gen. R. s. 32</cite> <he>אינו מספיק … עד שהיא פוֹקַעַת</he> he scarcely beats it (the bad flax) once, when it bursts; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 32">ib.</cite> s. 34; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 350">Yalk. Is. 350</cite>. Gen. R. l. c. <he>שאינו מקיש עליהם אחת עד שהיא פוקעת</he> he knocks at them (the bad earthen vessels) scarcely once, and one is cracked (ib. s. 32 <he>עד שהוא שוברם</he>).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Maasrot 3:2:3">Y. Maasr. III, 50ᵈ</cite> top <he>פעמים שהיא פוקעת וכ׳</he> sometimes it (the fig) bursts under the wheel.
<cite ref="Mishnah Zevachim 9:6">Zeb. IX, 6</cite> <he>גחלת שפָּקְעָה מעל וכ׳</he> a coal that sprang from the altar; <he>אברים שפָּקְעוּ וכ׳</he> chips of limbs that sprang off the altar.
<cite ref="Tosefta Parah 3:7">Tosef. Par. III</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Parah 2:11">II</cite>), 11 <he>פ׳ מעורה וכ׳</he> if a part of her skin … (in burning the red cow) leaped off beyond the pit.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 761:4">Yalk. Num. 761</cite> <he>את הפּוֹקְעִין</he> the portions which spring off, v. <cite ref="Q01504"><he>פֶּקַע</he></cite>; a. fr.—

Pesik. R. s. 11 או שמא תִפְקַע האוזן וכ׳ (or תִפָּקַע Nif.) or (I would venture to say it, were I not afraid,) lest the ear of the hearer burst, i.e. it is almost blasphemous to say it; (Mekh. Yithro, Baḥod., s. 2 כדי שתבקע אוזן it is enough for an ear to burst).

Y. Yeb. I, 2ᶜ bot. פקעו ממנה קידושין (not ופקעו) the betrothal rebounds from her, i.e. has no legal effect, opp. חלו עליה.—Part. pass. פָּקוּעַ; f. פְּקוּעָה an animal which is ripped open; בן (ה) פ׳ an animal taken alive out of the slaughtered mother’s womb.

senses.gloss: to cause splitting. Y. Pes. VII, 35ᵇ top שלא לפַקֵּעַ תחת הבשר in order not to cause a splitting of the bone under the flesh, v. פֶּקַע.

units: <cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 3:3">Sabb. III, 3</cite> (<cite ref="Shabbat 38b:10">38ᵇ</cite>) <he>לא יַפְקִיעֶנָּה בסודרין</he> he must not break it (the egg) over a hot cloth, Rashi (oth. interpret.: he must not cause it to crack by wrapping it in a hot cloth and rolling it; v. Tosaf. Yom Tob a. l.).

<cite ref="Beitzah 31b:9">Bets. 31ᵇ</cite> <he>מתיר ומַפְקִיעַ וחותך</he> may untie (the knot, v. <cite ref="H00498"><he>חוֹתָם</he></cite>), or ravel out or cut through; <cite ref="Shabbat 146a">Sabb. 146ᵃ</cite>; Y. ib. XV, beg. 15ᵃ, a. e. <he>ומַפְקִיעִין</he>, v. <cite ref="Q01511"><he>פִּקְפֵּק</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Sukkah 5:3">Succ. V, 3</cite> <he>מהן היו מַפְקִיעִין ובהן היו מדליקין</he> they stripped them (the worn-out belts of priests) and used them for wicks; <cite ref="Shabbat 21a:11">Sabb. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>בגדי … מפקיעין אותן ומהן היו עושין פתילות וכ׳</he> they ravelled out priestly garments and made of them wicks &c.; expl. Y. Succ. V, 55ᵇ bot. <he>מפשילים</he>, v. <cite ref="Q02083"><he>פָּשַׁל</he></cite>.

Esth. R. to I, 6 הכל מפקיעין בחבלי וכ׳ all make straps (for their couches) of woolen or flax ropes, and this wicked man uses byssus and purple; a. fr.—2) [to cause breaking loose,] to release, cancel an obligation.

<cite ref="Yevamot 66b">Yeb. 66ᵇ</cite> sq., a. fr. <he>הקדש … מפקיעין מידי שעבוד</he> consecration (of a pledged object), leavened matter (on the entrance of Passover), and liberation (of a pledged slave) cause a release from mortgage (cancel the mortgage contract).

<cite ref="Bekhorot 5a:9">Bekh. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>אין בכור מפקיע בכור</he> a first-born Levite could not serve as ransom for a first-born Israelite; <he>דיו לבכור שיַפְקִיעַ וכ׳</he> it was enough for the firstborn Levite that he released his own consecration (that he needed no priest to be substituted for him); a. fr.

senses.gloss: ה׳ השער to break up, unsettle the market, to raise prices arbitrarily, create a panic.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Taanit 2:9">Taan. II, 9</cite> <he>שלא להַפְקִיעַ השערים</he> in order not to cause a sudden rise of market prices (by creating the impression of impending scarcity).
<cite ref="Megillah 17b:15">Meg. 17ᵇ</cite> <he>כנגד מַפְקִיעֵי שערים</he> a prayer against those who raise prices (speculating on a coming scarcity).
